# 🔬 Research Identity

::: intro-block
**Urban Data Science · Imbalance-Aware Modelling · Reproducible AI Systems**

Jesús Cáceres-Tello is a researcher working at the intersection of urban sustainability, machine learning methodology, and open computational science.

His research focuses on the design and evaluation of predictive models under real-world constraints, particularly in environments characterised by class imbalance, temporal structure, and operational limitations.

Rather than prioritising algorithmic novelty, his work emphasises:
```{=html}
<ul>
  <li>Methodological rigour</li>
  <li>Time-aware validation</li>
  <li>Performance–cost trade-off analysis</li>
  <li>Reproducibility by design</li>
  <li>Open science integration</li>
</ul>
```
:::

# 🎯 Research Mission

The core objective of my research is to develop methodologically coherent AI frameworks for urban sustainability and STEM education.

This involves:
```{=html}
<ul>
  <li>Evaluating models under structural imbalance</li>
  <li>Designing reproducible analytical pipelines</li>
  <li>Integrating computational efficiency into model comparison</li>
  <li>Linking data science with institutional decision-making</li>
</ul>
```
My work contributes to a broader research programme in applied data science for sustainable systems, currently developed within my doctoral studies at the Complutense University of Madrid.
# 🔬 Research Areas

- 🌍 Urban environmental modelling and air quality forecasting
- ⚖️ Imbalanced learning and classification evaluation
- 🤖 Hybrid predictive architectures (Prophet–LSTM, GAT–BiLSTM)
- 📈 Performance–cost trade-off analysis
- 🧩 Open science and reproducible research infrastructures
- 🎓 AI-supported STEM education

# 🏗 Research Infrastructure & Open Science

All research projects are developed under a structured computational framework:
```{=html}
<ul>
  <li>Git-based version control</li>
  <li>Public repositories with DOI integration (Zenodo)</li>
  <li>Reproducible scripts and notebooks (R / Python / Quarto)</li>
  <li>Time-based validation strategies</li>
  <li>Transparent performance reporting</li>
</ul>
```
Each publication is accompanied by:
```{=html}
<ul>
  <li>An open repository</li>
  <li>Executable code</li>
  <li>Structured documentation</li>
  <li>Publicly accessible data sources</li>
</ul>
```
This approach ensures traceability, transparency, and methodological consistency across projects.

# 🎓 Academic Background & Professional Experience

Jesús Cáceres-Tello holds:
```{=html}
  <ul>
    <li>Diploma in Computer Science: University of Málaga</li>
    <li>B.Sc. in Computer Engineering: Catholic University of Ávila</li>
    <li>Master’s Degree in Educational Informatics: University of Alcalá</li>
    <li>He is currently pursuing a <strong>Ph.D. in Statistical Studies at the Complutense University of Madrid</strong>, developing methodological frameworks for urban sustainability analytics.</li>
  </ul>
<p>His professional experience includes:</p>
  <ul>
    <li>Leadership in university digital infrastructure systems</li>
    <li>Participation in European Electronic Health Record interoperability projects (ISO 13606, ISO 21090)</li>
    <li>Development of national e-learning platforms</li>
    <li>Public-sector environmental technology projects at Madrid City Council</li>
  </ul>
```
He has been teaching in higher education for over a decade and actively contributes to academic innovation initiatives.
